dictionary.Aircraft ID: The join key across every workbook in this set.
dictionary.Class: From wpcost unitClass: exp_fighter / exp_assault / exp_bomber.
dictionary.Gun Barrels: Total barrels across every mount, fixed and turret.
dictionary.Total Rounds: Every round carried across all guns.
dictionary.Burst Mass (kg/s): DERIVED: sum of (rate of fire / 60) x default shell mass across all barrels. A crude firepower proxy - it ignores filler, shell type and accuracy.
dictionary.Carries Guided Weapons: Heuristic on ordnance file names. Cross-check against the guided-weapon workbook rather than trusting this column alone.
dictionary.Gun Only: Yes means the aircraft references no ordnance file at all. These are the aircraft the weapon-centric workbook could not show.
dictionary.Sensor IDs: Join to the sensor workbook on Sensor ID.
dictionary.Performance Data: 'Own file', 'Shared flight model (x)' where it resolves through fmFile, or 'NOT IN THE FILES'. Half the roster is the last one - see READ ME.
dictionary.Top Speed (km/h): Best max speed across every tested altitude. Converted from m/s in the source.
dictionary.Top Speed At (m): The altitude that top speed occurs at.
dictionary.Best Climb (m/s): Best climb rate across tested altitudes - normally at sea level.
dictionary.Ceiling Tested To (m): Highest altitude the performance file carries data for. NOT the service ceiling.
dictionary.Repair Cost RB Upgraded (SL): repairCostFullUpgradedHistorical - what you actually pay once the aircraft is spaded.
dictionary.Avg Award RB (SL): avgAwardHistorical - what an average Realistic battle pays.
dictionary.Max Flight Time (min): Fuel-limited flight time at the default load.
dictionary.Cost per Sortie Ratio: DERIVED formula: upgraded repair cost divided by average award. Above 1.0 means an average battle does not pay for the repair.
dictionary.Barrels: How many of this gun type are fitted.
dictionary.Rounds Per Barrel: DERIVED: rounds carried divided by barrels.
dictionary.Mount: The trigger group: cannon, machine gun, gunner0 and so on.
dictionary.Turret Mounted: The mount has a turret block or a gunner trigger - defensive, not forward-firing.
dictionary.Belt Options: How many selectable belts the gun offers.
dictionary.Seconds of Fire: DERIVED: rounds per barrel divided by rounds per second. How long one barrel can fire continuously.
dictionary.Belt: The modification key inside the gun file.
dictionary.Shell Type: Raw bulletType - i_t, he_i, ap_i, aphe and so on.
dictionary.Incendiary Multiplier: onHitChanceMultFire - relative chance of starting a fire.
dictionary.Performance Source: Whether the row came from the aircraft's own file or a shared flight model.
dictionary.Optimal Speed (km/h): optSpeed - the speed the flight model treats as most efficient at that altitude.
dictionary.Ordnance File: Raw rocketgun or bombgun file name. Join to the guided-weapon workbook for missile detail.

readme: War Thunder — Aircraft: the full roster, guns included

The guided-weapon workbook is weapon-centric: one row per missile. A Bf 109, a Spitfire or a B-17 carries no guided weapon, so none of them appeared anywhere. This dataset is aircraft-centric - one row per aircraft - and ordnance becomes a child table joined on Aircraft ID.
116 units with unitMoveType 'helicopter' are deliberately out of scope.
!! PERFORMANCE DATA IS MISSING FOR HALF THE ROSTER !!
751 of 1440 aircraft have NO speed or climb figures. Those cells are blank and the Performance Data column says 'NOT IN THE FILES' in red.

Performance files exist almost entirely for propeller aircraft and early jets. Coverage by BR: 111 of 172 at BR 1.x, 139 of 190 at 2.x, dropping through the 6.x-8.x range, and ZERO above BR 10.0. Not one modern jet - no F-16, no MiG-29, no Su-27 - has a performance file.

The aero model for those aircraft lives in flightmodels/fm/ as a simulation input. Turning it into a top speed means running the flight model, which is a simulation, not an extraction. No figure has been invented.
Everything else: BR, class, crew, guns, ammunition, belts, ordnance, sensors, countermeasures and repair costs are complete for all 1,440 aircraft.
2192 aircraft-gun mounts covering 1395 aircraft and 347 distinct gun types. 5664 barrels in total.
7840 - bombs, rockets and missiles, joined on Aircraft ID.
592 carry no ordnance at all. These are exactly the aircraft the old workbook could not show.
FINDING THE GUNS WAS NOT STRAIGHTFORWARD

Fighters usually list guns inline under commonWeapons. Turret-armed bombers and many jets nest them under WeaponSlots -> WeaponPreset -> Weapon instead. Reading only commonWeapons found 1,176 mounts and missed every bomber turret; walking the whole definition found 2,192 mounts across 1,395 of 1,440 aircraft.
Flagged per mount, from the presence of a turret block or a gunner trigger.
DERIVED: sum over every barrel of (rate of fire / 60) x default shell mass. Kilograms of metal put out per second with everything firing.
Not damage. It ignores explosive filler, shell type and where the rounds land. It is a crude firepower proxy for comparing armament fits, nothing more.
Belt contents are listed per gun, not per aircraft. Which belts a given aircraft can research is in its modifications block and is not joined in yet.
Ordnance links are raw file references. Cross-reference the guided-weapon workbook on Aircraft ID for missile detail; bombs and rockets are listed by file name only.
45 aircraft resolve no guns. Some genuinely have none; some may declare them in a way this walk misses.
Repair costs and awards are Realistic values. Arcade and Simulator columns exist in the source but only RB is carried here.
START HERE. One row per aircraft: BR, class, crew, armament summary, performance where it exists, repair cost.
Every gun mount: barrels, rounds, rate of fire, seconds of continuous fire, turret flag.
The 347 distinct guns with calibre, rate of fire, mass and belt options.
What each belt actually contains - shell type, mass, velocity, filler.
Long format: aircraft x altitude x max speed, optimal speed, climb rate.
Which ordnance files each aircraft can carry. Join to the guided-weapon workbook here.
Radar, RWR and IRST fits. Join to the sensor workbook on Sensor ID.
Every column and its source key.
Aircraft ID is the key across all six workbooks. The guided-weapon workbook's Carriers sheet uses the same identifiers.
